param.reconstruction.keep_profile_cache_: Keep the internal U/R/F/M drizzle profile store after a finished image. Default: off (deleted). On = kept as a hashed cache so a re-fuse skips the forward-drizzle pass — costs disk. Does not change the computed result.
param.reconstruction.delete_source_cache: Delete the normalized CFA source cache and quality maps after a finished image. Default: off. On = frees disk immediately but DISABLES resume-reconstruction for this run (a later resume would re-normalize every frame). The report announces this as resume_reconstruction_disabled.
param.reconstruction.quality.pyramid.sca: Number of scales in the local quality maps; default: 4.

Controls how many spatial scales are used to measure each input frame's local quality. Fewer scales react more strongly to fine detail; more scales stabilize the estimate over larger nebula, background, and transparency structures. Higher values increase compute and cache work. Range: 1 to 8; default: 4.
param.reconstruction.quality.pyramid.bas: Window size in pixels on the finest quality scale.

Side length of the local measurement window on the finest scale of the quality maps. Smaller windows react more locally to fine detail but are noisier; larger windows smooth the estimate and lose local differences. Minimum: 1; default: 4.
param.reconstruction.quality.pyramid.sha: Weight of local sharpness in the quality score; default: 0.6.

Controls how strongly local sharpness contributes to the input frames' quality score. Higher values favor regions with better structural definition. Together with the SNR weight it sets the balance between resolution and noise stability; the sum of both weights must be greater than 0. Default: 0.6.
param.reconstruction.quality.pyramid.snr: Weight of the local signal-to-noise ratio; default: 0.4.
Controls how strongly the local signal-to-noise ratio contributes to the quality score. Higher values favor quieter, more stable regions; too high can downweight sharp but noisy detail. Default: 0.4.
param.reconstruction.quality.pyramid.sco: Steepness of the quality score sigmoid; default: 1.8.

Controls how strongly strong and weak image regions differ in the quality score. Higher values make the weighting more selective; lower values distribute weights more evenly. The score remains bounded to 0..1. Values must be greater than 0; default: 1.8.
param.reconstruction.quality.pyramid.art: Sigma threshold above which a region counts as artifact; default: 3.0.

Robust sigma threshold (MAD multiplier) for detecting suspicious deviations in the quality maps, such as satellite trails or cosmic-ray hits. Lower values mark more outliers and make the estimate stricter; higher values are more tolerant but may downweight weak artifacts less. Default: 3.0.
param.reconstruction.quality.pyramid.max: Maximum tolerated artifact fraction per measurement window; default: 0.25.

Sets how much suspicious pixel content a local measurement window tolerates before its quality score drops. Lower values react more strongly to trails, cloud residue, or registration errors. Range: greater than 0 to 1; default: 0.25.
param.reconstruction.delete_source_cache: Deletes the normalized CFA source cache and the quality maps after a fully committed final image. Frees disk space immediately but DISABLES reconstruction resume for this run — a later resume would have to re-normalize every frame. The report flags this as resume_reconstruction_disabled. Default: off.
param.reconstruction.keep_profile_cache_: Keeps the internal transactional U/R/F/M drizzle profile store after a committed final image as a hashed cache so a re-fuse can skip the forward-drizzle pass. Costs disk space; does not change the computed result. It is a reconstruction cache, never a resume predecessor. Default: off (deleted).
param.reconstruction.common_overlap_requ: Fraction of accepted frame footprints defining the analysis region; default: 1.0.

Fraction of accepted dense frame footprints that defines the common analysis region — independent of sparse CFA support. 1.0 requires full common coverage; lower values allow borders without full channel coverage. Range: (0, 1]; default: 1.0.
param.reconstruction.diagnostics.level.s: Scope of reconstruction diagnostics: summary or full; default: summary.
param.reconstruction.diagnostics.level.e: summary writes only the compact summary artifacts; full additionally writes verbose diagnostic output (more disk and I/O). Affects diagnostics only, not the image result. Default: summary.
param.reconstruction.diagnostics.preview: Opt-in stripe diagnostic of the uniform forward drizzle; writes summary statistics only; default: off.

Enables a bounded stripe diagnostic of the uniform (unweighted) forward-drizzle result. Writes summary statistics only — no complete reconstruction, no clipping, no multiband, no resume contract. Default: off.
param.reconstruction.diagnostics.persist: Persists unclipped uniform planes as immutable generations; default: off.

Opt-in, independent of preview: streams unclipped uniform planes into immutable generations under artifacts/forward_drizzle_uniform_store/; current.json atomically commits the complete generation after checksum and FITS validation. Reserves 8 MiB of I/O plus one float row in the drizzle budget; old generations are retained. Diagnostic only, not a resume entry. Default: off.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.internal_sc: Internal upsampling factor of the drizzle grid (1 or 2); default: 2.

Factor by which the internal forward-drizzle accumulation grid is upsampled relative to the input grid. 2 allows finer drop placement and sharper reconstruction at significantly more memory and compute; 1 works on the native grid. Enum: 1 or 2; default: 2.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.output_scal: Scale factor of the output image (1 or 2); default: 1.
Sets the scale factor of the result image. 1 = native output; 2 = double output resolution with significantly larger files and more compute. Enum: 1 or 2; default: 1.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.kernel.shor: Footprint shape of the drizzle drops; currently only square; default: square.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.kernel.expl: Shape of the drop footprint with which each input pixel is projected onto the output grid. Only square is currently implemented. Default: square.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.pixfrac.sho: Linear size of the drizzle drop relative to the input pixel; default: 0.8.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.pixfrac.exp: Scales the edge length of the projected drop (classic drizzle pixfrac). Smaller values sharpen the reconstruction and act more selectively but can amplify holes and aliasing; larger values smooth more and fill gaps more reliably. Range: greater than 0 to 1; default: 0.8.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.robust_pass: Number of robust re-weighting passes; default: 2.
How often robust accumulation with updated outlier rejection is repeated. More passes stabilize outlier detection but cost additional compute. Range: 1 to 6; default: 2.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.min_clip_co: Minimum number of contributions per pixel before sigma clipping applies; default: 5.

Below this contribution count no clipping is performed because the statistics would be too thin — the pixel is accumulated unclipped. Higher values make clipping more conservative. Minimum: 2; default: 5.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.full_frame_: Let every frame, not only the reservoir, determine the value; default: off.

By default the per-pixel value comes from the hash-selected reservoir frames (at most 64), however many frames were streamed. When enabled, those frames only define the sigma-clip bounds (pilot); every other frame's folded candidate is then tested against the frozen bounds and accumulated, which lowers noise for long series. Runs on CPU and CUDA and reads quality maps for all frames, so it costs additional time. Works only with wide symmetric clip bounds (about clip_sigma_low = clip_sigma_high = 4); with the asymmetric 2/4 the gain is small. The code and schema default is off; the shipped tile_compile.yaml turns it on together with clip 4/4. Requires multiband to be enabled.
Target rows per processing stripe; 0 = automatic; default: 0.
Target row count per stripe; 0 selects at most 256 rows within the memory budget. Explicit values exceeding the budget fail closed. Minimum: 0; default: 0.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.chunk_halo_: Exact source-footprint enumeration completes each target stripe without an output halo; the CPU uniform/coverage path does not duplicate halo rows. Minimum: -1; default: -1.
param.reconstruction.drizzle.memory_budg: Phase memory budget in MiB; 0 inherits runtime_limits.memory_budget; default: 0.

Phase allocation budget in MiB including retained masks/output, one source plus transient load copy and stripe scratch. 0 inherits runtime_limits.memory_budget (library default 512 MiB); available host/cgroup headroom may reduce it. Fails before allocation if one row does not fit. Minimum: 0; default: 0.
param.reconstruction.clipping.clip_sigma: Lower sigma threshold of robust clipping; default: 3.0.
Contributions below the lower sigma bound are rejected. Lower values cut more aggressively (dark outliers, underexposure); higher values are more tolerant. Greater than 0; default: 3.0.
Upper sigma threshold of robust clipping; default: 3.0.
Contributions above the upper sigma bound are rejected — typical hits are satellite and airplane trails, hot pixels and cosmic rays. Lower values reject more strictly. Greater than 0; default: 3.0.
param.reconstruction.clipping.min_fracti: Fraction of contributions that must remain per pixel after clipping; default: 0.4.
Veto bound: if clipping discards more than (1 − min_fraction) of a pixel's contributions, the clip is considered too aggressive and fails. Range: greater than 0 to 1; default: 0.4.
Minimum effective sample count per pixel after clipping; default: 3.0.

Veto bound: if fewer than min_n_eff effective contributions remain after clipping, the clip fails. Together with min_fraction it protects against overly aggressive rejection on thin stacks. Minimum: 1; default: 3.0.
param.reconstruction.clipping.guard_fall: On veto failure use the clip survivors (or unclipped candidates); default: off.

If the min_fraction/min_n_eff veto fails, the enabled fallback uses the sigma-clip survivors (or, if none survived, every original candidate unclipped) instead of leaving the pixel/channel unsupported. Default: off — preserves the exact reviewed 8-step procedure.
param.reconstruction.clipping.shared_fra: Reconcile per-channel clip decisions across R/G/B against anti-correlated CFA chroma noise; default: off.

Each channel's sigma clip decides independently which frames are outliers; since R/G/B are sampled from disjoint sensor pixels, this can reject a frame in one channel while keeping it in another, producing anti-correlated chroma speckle. When enabled, a frame is rejected in every channel that saw it as a candidate once the fraction of those channels that independently rejected it exceeds shared_frame_rejection_consensus. A frame seen by only one channel is left untouched. Runs on both the CPU and CUDA backends. Default: off.
param.reconstruction.clipping.bimodal_ve: Rejects a coherent minority population the ordinary wide clip bound alone admits; default: off.

After the asymmetric median/MAD clip pass converges, checks the accepted set for a coherent second population the ordinary bound alone did not separate from the majority (e.g. a subset of frames with a small but real registration/tracking offset at this exact pixel), more likely with wide clip_sigma_low/clip_sigma_high. If the largest gap between consecutive accepted values exceeds bimodal_veto_gap_sigma times the pass's own MAD and splits off a minority side of at least 2 candidates holding less than half the accepted weight, that minority is dropped. Runs on both the CPU and CUDA backends. Default: off.
Multiple of the clip pass's MAD the largest accepted-value gap must exceed to count as bimodal; range: > 0. Default: 2.5.

Sets how large the largest gap between consecutive accepted values must be, relative to the clip pass's own MAD, before bimodal_veto treats the split as a coherent second population rather than ordinary spread. Lower values fire more readily. Only meaningful when bimodal_veto is enabled. Range: > 0. Default: 2.5.
param.reconstruction.clipping.shared_fra: Fraction of candidate-seeing channels that must reject a frame before shared_frame_rejection drops it everywhere; range: (0, 1]. Default: 0.5.

Threshold on the rejection fraction across the channels that saw a given frame as a clip candidate. 0.5 means a simple majority; 1.0 effectively disables the consensus revision (bit-identical to shared_frame_rejection: off). Only meaningful when shared_frame_rejection is enabled. Default: 0.5.
param.reconstruction.coverage_gate.min_f: Minimum number of registered frames per channel; default: 2.
The coverage gate aborts the run when a channel delivers fewer registered contributions. Protects against reconstructions from too thin material. Minimum: 2; default: 2.
param.reconstruction.coverage_gate.min_s: Minimum fraction of the output area with sufficient sample coverage; default: 0.995.
Fraction of the common overlap area that must be supported by enough samples per channel. Values below 1 tolerate small uncovered borders. Range: greater than 0 to 1; default: 0.995.
param.reconstruction.coverage_gate.min_c: Absolute lower bound of the effective sample count per channel; default: 3.0.

Each channel's effective sample count (10th percentile) must reach at least this value — the effective bound is the maximum of this absolute floor and min_channel_n_eff_fraction × total count. Minimum: 1; default: 3.0.
Fraction of the total sample count each channel must at least deliver; default: 0.15.

Relative lower bound: a channel's effective sample count must reach at least this fraction of the total contribution count. Prevents a channel with almost no contributions from entering the reconstruction. Range: greater than 0 to 1; default: 0.15.
param.reconstruction.coverage_gate.min_a: Minimum number of analyzable pixels for the coverage analysis; default: 1024.
With fewer analyzable pixels the coverage decision is flagged as insufficiently supported (insufficient_analysis_support) instead of producing a reliable verdict. Minimum: 1; default: 1024.
param.reconstruction.coverage_gate.max_i: Maximum tolerated contiguous hole area without coverage in pixels; 0 = none; default: 0.
Largest allowed contiguous area without sample coverage inside the overlap. 0 requires gapless coverage; larger values tolerate small holes. Minimum: 0; default: 0.
param.reconstruction.multiband.enabled.s: Enables multiband fusion (frequency-band-dependent quality weighting); default: on.
param.reconstruction.multiband.enabled.e: Switches multiband fusion on: the quality maps act separately on fine and medium frequency bands so local sharpness is weighted more strongly than smooth areas. Off = uniform quality weighting across all bands. Default: on.
param.reconstruction.multiband.levels.sh: Number of à-trous decomposition levels; default: 3.
param.reconstruction.multiband.levels.ex: Depth of the wavelet-like band decomposition for multiband fusion. More levels separate fine from coarse structures more precisely but cost compute and memory. Range: 1 to 4; default: 3.
param.reconstruction.multiband.alpha_cap: Upper bound of the multiband blend factor; default: 1.0.
Caps the fraction by which the quality-weighted solution overrides the uniform solution. Values below 1 make the fusion more conservative and dampen possible artifacts. Range: 0 to 1; default: 1.0.
param.reconstruction.multiband.fine_qual: Quality exponent of the finest band; default: 4.0.

The fine band weighting scales with quality^exponent. Higher values differentiate more strongly between good and poor areas in the detail band; lower values distribute weights more evenly. Minimum: 0; default: 4.0.
param.reconstruction.multiband.medium_qu: Quality exponent of the medium bands; default: 2.0.
Like the fine-band exponent but for the medium frequency bands. Typically lower so large-scale structure stays more robust than detail sharpness. Minimum: 0; default: 2.0.
param.reconstruction.multiband.min_quali: Lower threshold of quality separation for band blending; default: 0.05.
Below this quality separation the evidence is not distinct enough and blending stays restrained (smoothstep lower edge). Range: 0 to 1; default: 0.05.
param.reconstruction.multiband.full_qual: Above this quality separation blending applies fully; default: 0.2.
Upper edge of the smoothstep ramp: above this quality separation the separation factor reaches its maximum. Must be greater than min_quality_separation. Range: 0 to 1; default: 0.2.
param.reconstruction.multiband.min_effec: Lower threshold of effective sample count for blending; default: 8.0.
Below this effective contribution count multiband blending stays restrained because the statistics are too thin (smoothstep lower edge). Minimum: 1; default: 8.0.
param.reconstruction.multiband.full_effe: Above this effective sample count blending applies fully; default: 24.0.
Upper edge of the smoothstep ramp over the effective sample count: above this value the n_eff factor reaches its maximum. Must be greater than min_effective_samples. Minimum: 1; default: 24.0.
ui.jev.object_class.label: Object class
ui.jev.tooltip.object_class: Your statement about the target. Some recommendations (e.g. denoise, background) depend on it; without it they abstain.
param.hypermetric_stretch.large_scale_co: Lifts only the large-scale sky structure (dust lanes, reflection nebulae) of the stretched image without amplifying noise, stars or fine detail; default: off.

The global stretch curve squeezes faint, extended sky structure into a very narrow band above the background. This stage lifts only that large-scale component: the luminance is reduced to a star-free coarse map (masked downsampling, 5x5 median, masked Gaussian of sigma_px) and its deviation from the sky level (median over the valid area) is added back scaled by `amount`: I' = I + amount*(LS(I) - sky), the same delta on R, G and B. Noise, star profiles and fine detail stay unchanged (tested on IC4605: pixel noise x1.000, star width x1.000, star signal x1.000, sky structure x1.8 to x3.3 for amount 1 to 3). A flat image is unchanged, pixels outside the valid mask are never touched, values stay within [0, per-channel maximum of the input]. Runs after the colour-cast correction. Default: off.
Factor on the large-scale luminance deviation from the sky; 1 doubles, 2 triples the visible structure; range [0, 6]; default: 1.0.

Factor on the large-scale deviation from the sky level: 0 = nothing, 1 = double, 2 = triple the visible structure (at sigma_px 48 the coarse map of a broad structure carries about 60 % of its amplitude, so the gain is correspondingly smaller). Higher values also lift residual sky gradients; see `remove_vignette` for a vignette and BGE for light-pollution gradients. Range [0, 6]. Default 1.0.
Sigma of the "large" component in output pixels; smaller structure is left alone; range (0, 512]; default: 48.

Scale of the "large" component (Gaussian sigma in output pixels). Structure smaller than about this value is not lifted. Internally about sigma_px/6 pixels per cell (1 to 16) are used. Small values approach a local contrast; 32 to 96 suit dust lanes and reflection nebulae. Range (0, 512]. Default 48.
Same factor for the large-scale colour differences R-G and B-G (G unchanged); 0 = colour unchanged; range [0, 6]; default: 0.

Like `amount`, but for the large-scale colour differences R-G and B-G; G stays the reference channel and never changes, the luminance structure is untouched. Brings out large-scale colour structure (e.g. yellow reflection nebulae against blue dust lanes). Range [0, 6]. Default 0 (colour unchanged).
Keeps a radially symmetric component (vignette, radial sky glow) out of the boost; default: on.

Before the boost a radially symmetric component (robust polynomial in r^2 about the centre of the valid area) is removed from the deviation. Without flat-field calibration the vignette is part of the large-scale structure and would be amplified together with the nebula (test: vignette x(1 + amount) without, below x1.5 with this option). Off-centre nebulae are kept. For a centred, radially symmetric object the option can remove structure too; turn it off then. Default: on.
